pyqs.pyq_content: <prep-p>$$ \int_{\frac{-\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sin ^{-4} x d x= $$</prep-p>
pyqs.explanation_content:
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} &\text {} \begin{aligned} Let \,\,\, I & =\int_{-\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}(\sin x)^{-4} d x \\ & =2 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}(\sin x)^{-4} d x \end{aligned}\\ &\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\ldots\left[\because(\sin x)^{-4} \text { is an even function }\right] \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} &\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, =2 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{1}{\sin ^4 x} \mathrm{~d} x \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, =2 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{\sec ^4 x}{\tan ^4 x} \mathrm{~d} x \\ &\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,  =2 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right) \sec ^2 x}{\tan ^4 x} \mathrm{~d} x \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>Put $\tan x=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow \sec ^2 x \mathrm{~d} x=\mathrm{dt}$</prep-p>
<prep-p>When $x=0, \mathrm{t}=0$ and when $x=\frac{\pi}{4}, \mathrm{t}=1$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad I & =2 \int_0^1 \frac{1+t^2}{t^4} d t \\ & =2\left[\int_0^1 \frac{1}{t^4} d t+\int_0^1 \frac{1}{t^2} d t\right]=2\left[\frac{\left[t^{-3}\right]_0^1}{-3}+\frac{\left[t^{-1}\right]_0^1}{-1}\right]=\frac{-8}{3} \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>

pyqs.pyq_content: <prep-p>The area bounded by the curve $x=2-y-y^2$ and the Y -axis is</prep-p>
pyqs.explanation_content:
<prep-p>Given equation of curve</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} & x=2-y-y^2 \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,...(i)\\ & \text { Y-axis } \Rightarrow x=0 \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>Put $x=0$, in equation (i), we get</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} & 0=2-y-y^2 \\ & \Rightarrow y^2+y-2=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(y+2)(y-1)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y+2=0 \text { or } y=1 \\ & \Rightarrow y=-2 \text { or } y=1 \\ & \text { Required area }=\int_{y=a}^b \mathrm{f}(y) \mathrm{d} y \\ & =\int_{-2}^1\left(2-y-y^2\right) \mathrm{d} y \\ & =\left[2 y-\frac{y^2}{2}-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^1 \\ & =\left(2-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right)-\left(-4-\frac{4}{2}+\frac{8}{3}\right) \\ & =\left(\frac{12-3-2}{6}\right)-\left(\frac{-24-12+16}{6}\right) \\ & =\frac{7}{6}-\frac{(-20)}{6} \\ & =\frac{27}{6}=\frac{9}{2} \text { sq. units. } \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>

pyqs.pyq_content: <prep-p>The area of the region bounded by $\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1$ and the line $\frac{x}{3}+\frac{y}{2}=1$ is</prep-p>
pyqs.explanation_content:
<prep-img src="https://app-content.cdn.examgoal.net/fly/@width/image/jaoe38c1mesvazbi/2f23c3ed-ccc3-4866-8d97-ea780b9709f6/cd7726e0-82a8-11f0-8f03-a319c67d38be/file-jaoe38c1mesvazd5.png?format=png" data-orsrc="https://app-content.cdn.examgoal.net/image/jaoe38c1mesvazbi/2f23c3ed-ccc3-4866-8d97-ea780b9709f6/cd7726e0-82a8-11f0-8f03-a319c67d38be/file-jaoe38c1mesvazd5.png" loading="lazy" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-height: 40vh; vertical-align: baseline" alt="MHT CET 2025 20th April Morning Shift Mathematics - Area Under The Curves Question 13 English Explanation">
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} &\text { Required area }=\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{OACB})-\mathrm{A}(\triangle \mathrm{OAB})\\ &\text { Given equation of ellipse is } \frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1\\ &\begin{array}{ll} \therefore & \frac{y^2}{4}=1-\frac{x^2}{9} \\ \therefore & y=\frac{2}{3} \sqrt{9-x^2} \\ & \mathrm{~A}(\mathrm{OACB})=\int_0^3 \frac{2}{3} \sqrt{9-x^2} \mathrm{~d} x \\ & =\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{1}{2} x \sqrt{9-x^2}+\frac{9}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{x}{3}\right]_0^3 \\ & =\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \sqrt{9-3^2}+\frac{9}{2} \sin ^{-1} \frac{3}{3}-\frac{1}{2} 0 \sqrt{9-0^2}-\frac{9}{2} \sin ^{-1} 0\right] \\ & =\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{9}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{3 \pi}{2} \\ & \mathrm{~A}(\Delta \mathrm{OAB})=\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 2=3 \\ \therefore & \text { Required area }=\frac{3 \pi}{2}-3=\frac{3}{2}(\pi-2) \text { sq. units } \end{array} \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>Alternate method:</prep-p>
<prep-p>The area between $\frac{x^2}{\mathrm{a}^2}+\frac{y^2}{\mathrm{~b}^2}=1$ and straight line $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$ is $\frac{1}{4} \pi a b-\frac{1}{2} a b$ sq. units.</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \text { Required area } & =\frac{1}{4} \pi(3)(2)-\frac{1}{2}(3)(2) \\ & =\frac{3}{2}(\pi-2) \text { sq. units } \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>

pyqs.pyq_content: <prep-p>The solution of the differential equation $(1+x) \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}-x y=1-x$ is</prep-p>
pyqs.a: <prep-p>$y(1+x)=x+\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration</prep-p>
pyqs.b: <prep-p>$\quad y(1+x)=\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration</prep-p>
pyqs.c: <prep-p>$y(1-x)=x-\mathrm{ce}^x$, where c is the constant of integration</prep-p>
pyqs.d: <prep-p>$y(1+x)=x$, where c is the constant of integration</prep-p>
pyqs.explanation_content: <prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{ll}  & (1+x) \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}-x y=1-x \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{\mathrm{~d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}-\left(\frac{x}{1+x}\right) y=\frac{1-x}{1+x} \\ \therefore \quad & \text { I. F. }=\mathrm{e}^{-\int \frac{x}{1+x} \mathrm{dx}} \\ = & \mathrm{e}^{\int\left(-1+\frac{1}{1+x}\right) \mathrm{dx}} \\ = & \mathrm{e}^{-x+\log (1+x)} \\ = & \mathrm{e}^{-x} \mathrm{e}^{\log (1+x)} \\ = & \mathrm{e}^{-x}(1+x) \end{array}\\ &\therefore \quad \text { Solution of the given equation is }\\ &\begin{aligned} & y(1+x) \mathrm{e}^{-x}=\int\left(\frac{1-x}{1+x}\right)(1+x) \mathrm{e}^{-x} \mathrm{~d} x+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow y(1+x) \mathrm{e}^{-x}=\int(1-x) \mathrm{e}^{-x} \mathrm{~d} x+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow y(1+x) \mathrm{e}^{-x}=\int \mathrm{e}^{-x} \mathrm{~d} x-\int x \mathrm{e}^{-x} \mathrm{~d} x+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow y(1+x) \mathrm{e}^{-x}=-\mathrm{e}^{-x}-\left(-x \mathrm{e}^{-x}-\mathrm{e}^{-x}\right)+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow y(1+x) \mathrm{e}^{-x}=x \mathrm{e}^{-x}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow y(1+x)=x+c \mathrm{e}^x \end{aligned} \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
pyqs.sub_topics: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

pyqs.pyq_content: <prep-p>The population of towns A and B increase at the rate proportional to their population present at that time. At the end of the year 1984, the population of both the towns was 20,000 . At the end of the year 1989, the population of town A was 25,000 and that of town B was 28,000 . The difference of populations of towns A and B at the end of 1994 was</prep-p>
pyqs.explanation_content:
<prep-p>Let $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}$ be the populations of town A and town $B$ at time $t$ years, respectively.</prep-p>
<prep-p>Then, $\frac{d P_A}{d t}=k_1 P_A$ and $\frac{d P_B}{d t}=k_2 P_B$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dP}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}}=\mathrm{k}_1 \mathrm{dt}$ and $\frac{\mathrm{dP}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\mathrm{k}_2 \mathrm{dt}$</prep-p>
<prep-p>Integrating on both sides, we get</prep-p>
<prep-p>$\log P_A=k_1 t+c_1$ and</prep-p>
<prep-p>$\log \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{k}_2 \mathrm{t}+\mathrm{c}_2$</prep-p>
<prep-p>When $\mathrm{t}=0, \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=20,000$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{array}{ll} \therefore \quad & \log 20000=\mathrm{c}_1 \text { and } \\ \therefore \quad & \log 20000=\mathrm{c}_2 \\ & \log \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{k}_1 \mathrm{t}+\log 20000 \text { and } \\ & \log \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{k}_2 \mathrm{t}+\log 20000 \\ & \Rightarrow \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}}{20000}\right)=\mathrm{k}_1 \mathrm{t} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,...(i)\\ & \text { and } \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}}{20000}\right)=\mathrm{k}_2 \mathrm{t} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,...(ii)\end{array} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>Town A:</prep-p>
<prep-p>When $\mathrm{t}=1989-1984=5, \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}=25,000$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \therefore \quad \log \left(\frac{25000}{20000}\right)=5 \mathrm{k}_1 $$         …[From (i)]</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow k_1=\frac{1}{5} \log \left(\frac{5}{4}\right) \\ \therefore \quad & \log \left(\frac{P_A}{20000}\right)=\frac{t}{5} \log \left(\frac{5}{4}\right)\,\,\,\, …[From (i)] \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} & \text { When } t=1994-1984=10 \\ & \log \left(\frac{P_A}{20000}\right)=\frac{10}{5} \log \left(\frac{5}{4}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \log \left(\frac{P_A}{20000}\right)=2 \log \left(\frac{5}{4}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{P_A}{20000}=\frac{25}{16} \\ & \Rightarrow P_A=31,250 \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>Town B:</prep-p>
<prep-p>When $\mathrm{t}=1989-1984=5, \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=28,000$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \therefore \quad \log \left(\frac{28000}{20000}\right)=5 \mathrm{k}_2\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,. . .[\text { From (ii)] } $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}_2=\frac{1}{5} \log \left(\frac{7}{5}\right) \\ \therefore & \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}}{20000}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{t}}{5} \log \left(\frac{7}{5}\right) \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,. . .[\text { From (ii)] }\end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
<prep-p>$$ \begin{aligned} &\begin{aligned} & \text { When } t=1994-1984=10 \\ & \log \left(\frac{P_B}{20000}\right)=\frac{10}{5} \log \left(\frac{7}{5}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \log \left(\frac{P_B}{20000}\right)=2 \log \left(\frac{7}{5}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{P_B}{20000}=\frac{49}{25} \\ & \Rightarrow P_B=39,200 \end{aligned}\\ &\therefore \quad \text { Difference of populations }\\ &=39200-31250=7950 \end{aligned} $$</prep-p>
